body: As this has passed community approval in its current form, wanted to say well done to Thom and agency team, looking forward to how things develop :)

i think this is a reasonable request in that we need some in an operational level that is incentivized to focus on Edgeware. 
I dont know any any of history thats being discussed here and frankly not interested in reading through it... 
If someone is asking for funds to help provide key operational infrastructure afloat this is a fair ask. The reality is the journey to decentralization is taking place as we see more participants get invovled in conversation, governance, working groups and while we may not be in the ideal place. There is the agency to help steward this in the time being. 
That said, i think this is a reasonable request and is in like w/ our overall goals.

Social media has been affecting people's way of thinking. Their algorithms want you to think/decide in binaries i.e. either of right/wrong, success/failure, good/bad, etc. (In the long term this will help those backend algorithms to precisely predict the individual human behaviour/nature.)

We as a community should start thinking about successes and failures as a collective result of all contributions. If you think this way, the argument of taking credit for external factors fails immediately.

For example: If recruiting Filip Kalebo as the runtime developer is considered a collective success, the credit goes to every active contributor of all scales that helped to make/keep the Edgeware ecosystem interesting for new devs and that includes Agency too.

I agree that we should see this all as a collective effort, the key is some people are paid for their contributions and difficult as it is, we need a way to assign credit in some specific ways else how do we judge relative success given specific deliverables. The more general we get the more subjective it becomes. 

For example, if one project fails to deliver, but it was funded at a point when others did, should the failed project claim others success? Equally, when EDG pumped on the back of the news about the EDGE gamers, can people claim that as successful? 

This is why smaller more focused projects makes more sense than one monolithic organisation which attempts to cover all areas - the simple fact is, it is very hard to assign success, unless there are direct metrics that qualify that success. 

The only reason I mentioned social media and Kabocha, is there is a very easy way to qualify that claim (although it is not perfect) and that is down to the social conversation and media coverage. Of course arrivals to Edgeware may be entirely unrelated to Kabocha, but given there has been no Edgeware output in the media or social content, it seems intuitive to assign the growth to that.

**Disclaimer: I like the Kabocha project and I also admire the contributions by Ramsey but your reasoning continuously pushed me to compare this proposal with Kabocha's technical steward grant. I also admire the work of the GMI media podcast team. This is not a personal attack on anyone including you Rich. I hope these comments/reasonings will be taken with sporting spirit. I also appreciate any constructive criticism on any of the points. Apologies in advance if I stated any incorrect information. **

**Reasons for comparing Kabocha's technical steward grant and other proposals:**
- Kabocha's technical steward grant is bigger than the agency's funding and the recipient is a single entity with a single individual. Why it was not broken down into small technical deliverables further? Especially milestone 2 and milestone 3 are basically the same deliverables with double rewards. It doesn't make sense at all to count them as two different milestones. In the case of double rewards, the recipient is usually offered one of those rewards as per their choice. This approach also makes sense as there are no technical deliverables in milestone 3.
- There is no precise information on whether milestone 3 will be proposed after the democracy. If not, this makes the distribution piechart ethically incorrect. If you have already decided on the 3% as the "KAB genesis maintainers stake", it's better to be represented in the piechart else it becomes a misleading representation. Earlier in one of the community calls, you asked why I didn't raise these issues before? Well, I had no problem at all with milestone 1 and I voted/supported the milestone 1 proposal only.
- Unlike the milestone 1 technical steward proposal, the agency funding got community-mandate on 1 year of operations. And I did ask publicly what if the funds extinct earlier than 1 year in case of the bearish market and if I am not wrong, you only did answer something similar to "We propose for more until we complete the 1 year". I saw you referred 25M EDG a lot of times instead of 120k USD. Will your reaction be different if the EDG price were 10 times than current one and if the top-up request was for 2.5M EDG?
- The above logic also opens up concerns if you delayed all these proposals intentionally due to the price pump because of the Edward Gaming event. The podcast team reported you the short of funding 5 months before you proposed the top-up v1 proposal. Weirdly they took 2 months to calculate how much extra they need and even after that you took 3 more months to propose the v1 top-up proposal!
- You're supportive of 100k USD funding for simple integration and not supportive of 120k USD funding for 4 months of operations based on the salaries of 8 Agency members. As an NSP, you should have the same standards for the proposals you curate and also the proposals you don't curate.


**What points you're missing on:**
- Truly sustainable operations of an existing chain are way more challenging than just the technical part of launching a new chain.
- Most of the operational deliverables don't have direct success-judging parameters.
- Your point of breaking down this proposal into small proposals of all the 8 agency members as solo contributors is exactly what we will be doing after the conclusion of 1-year pre-approved community mandate. (We call it decentralisation of agency.)
- Again, this is not an extension proposal but a top-up proposal based on the previously community-approved proposal by the Agency for 1 year of the operations.

[strangely enough, it doesn't look like I can reply to Shankar's last comment but only to the parent]
All the debate about whether the agency has been optimally useful or not, and what needs to be changed is a crucial question indeed, but it is almost orthogonal. I think this discussion ought to happen more efficiently when people from the agency will submit their proposals for the next period as they see fit.
But I think this specific proposal is in fact quite simple: we had the agency funded for one year, and it happened that price drop, excess costs, external circumstances, whatever that is explained above caused it to run out of funds before the deadline.
There is now a topup required to pay people, and a cost associated to it: 125K USD for 8 people for 4 months.
So the question is: do we topup to pay people or not?

Further point on documentation. This is basic stuff. 

> **Review the deliverables, and search the docs for the specific items that were promised, and you will find them. Cameron delivered these. Sorry that they may not be to your aesthetic preferences.**

The intro here: [https://docs.edgeware.wiki/readme-1/why-develop-on-edgeware](https://docs.edgeware.wiki/readme-1/why-develop-on-edgeware)

It is completely out of date and still focuses on Dillon's post on parachain bonding.

https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/830-draft-proposal-edgeware-parachain-bonding

You misinterpret my stance. I'm not dismissing -- nor 'avoiding conversation,' (This thread is open for all!) I am letting our work speak for itself, and the community will decide whether it was worth it. It will allow us to continue paying our staff to perform the day-to-day operations of community, finance, infrastructure, etc.

You seem to be in the process of revising history:

- "Marketing / narrative development has happened primarily externally"
- **How so? Johan, Jan, myself, Shankar, gmeister7, and everyone at the Thursday calls have been writing, tweeting, etc. Blog.edgewa.re is full of our work. We did test the 2 months of marketing services, and I ended the contract. Everything else has been us. **


- Runtime developer was recruited externally
- **Flipchan showed up in our chat rooms, he was not recruited in the traditional sense of external**. A community member and NSP took the initiative to perform the governance process. That community member was also an Agency member and developed their NSP concept, as you admit, under the experience you had while in the Agency. I specifically note in the deliverables that you brought forward the proposal and managed his onboard. 


- Parachain strategy and implementation has happened externally
- **Very misleading.  See **[https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/discussion/1415-request-for-a-community-parachain](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/discussion/1415-request-for-a-community-parachain) **You've drawn on the work of CW and MYSELF,  you've drawn on the time the Agency spent strategizing as a group. Just because you went and did a very different thing than anyone imagined or initially planned doesn't mean you get to ignore standing on the shoulders of others.**


- Grant proposals have been developed externally
- **I don't even know what your point is here --  that the Agency did not sponsor and mange 100% of grants? I wrote the templates. We have sponsored MANY. We have trained MANY. We remain a core governance asset. **


- Documentation remains poor and outdated.
- **Review the deliverables, and search the docs for the specific items that were promised, and you will find them. Cameron delivered these. Sorry that they may not be to your aesthetic preferences.**



I will not be going back and forth on this before waiting to bring it on-cha

I know the answer is you would rather get this through and people paid which I completely understand, but this is not a 'rolling contract' that just needs rubber stamping.

As by far the best paid and experienced member of the Edgeware community you should not avoid this debate, but encourage it. That is what a leader does.

full_text:
Thanks [@Thom Ivy](/edgeware/account/jKauGVPCQkteGTDKuuNwhYhMBrj5QuytgybEC4A5cS4Bki5) 

The Agency has been by far and away the biggest deployment of community funds to date (49M EDG) and therefore the biggest experiment in decentralised funding, therefore it is vital that we dig deeper into what worked and didn't rather than just rolling along into more funding without a critical analysis. 

Since that funding we have also evolved as a community, with new contributors, members and projects so it's worth going back to the start to share our learnings and where this proposal came from. 

The following as a critique of the proposal and the agency model in general not a personal criticism. 

Given I was part of the Agency proposal and team and received funds for a few months I have experienced all sides of this and indeed the creation of the Network Services model was a direct result of seeing the fundamental issues with delegating a large amount of funds for a wide range of tasks to a small number of individuals in a decentralised network. 

## Initial thesis

From the original [Agency proposal](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/discussion/1112-proposal-edgeware-agency-funding):

> Edgeware, unlike most chains, did not have a centralized launch. As a result, it also does not have a traditional foundation empowered to sign contracts, pay traditional companies, or conduct basic business activities. Commonwealth Labs, who helped coordinate the launch of Edgeware and has thus far solely supported the development of the chain and several business development functions, is now ready to focus on specific applications on Edgeware. 

Further...

> Without this entity, we will currently have no group that markets, coordinates, manages news, media, or guides interested projects on grant proposals, facilitates community engineering tasks, supports setting strategies, or cat-herds our several projects and large community. 

The primary issues that the Agency was founded to address were:

- Develop and implement marketing strategies
- Recruit core runtime development talent 
- Develop parachain strategy
- Address EDG liquidity via listings and market making 
- Guide grant proposals
- Manage / develop community assets
- Website
- Documentation
- Apps 
- Coordinate more general community activities.


You can view how these are broken down in the [Agency deliverables](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MFX8mCvkuXHXmrEaG19wbhZYyqbiVrRcEW2WfuzShSQ/edit#gid=0)  

Having been on the inside of the operation and having developed many proposals for the chain now, I can attest to how bewildering the workload is and how things that should take a few days often take weeks or months. 

## Successes / Failures

In some areas the Agency has excelled - namely coordinating calls, opening up the Discord and developing talent who are now setting out to develop their own proposals. 

In many of the fundamental deliverables, it has not been successful and to claim credit is misleading. 

- Marketing / narrative development has happened primarily externally
- Runtime developer was recruited externally 
- Parachain strategy and implementation has happened externally
- Grant proposals have been developed externally
- Documentation remains poor and outdated


The primary issue is that no one person can possibly cover off all of this and hope to keep their head above water - instead you are constantly pulled in many directions, whilst attempting to be a 'leader' in a network of your peers.

It is an impossible task that spreads time too thin and inevitably to burn out.

The solution is indeed the decentralisation of the team and the packaging up of core issues into working groups and specific project teams, each focused on a tight remit to address and build against a clear scope. 

As you can see from Kabocha, we are pulling apart all the constituent elements of the new network and turning each into a specific proposal with focused responsibilities that then have their own agency (pun intended). 

The creation of the Network Services model exists to target the basic issues, before recruiting talent / developing proposals and  stewarding them to completion - alongside ensuring there is consistent communication between the groups, whilst giving them complete autonomy.

The financial remuneration is clear - 10% on top of an approved proposal, the incentives are clear. 

## Summary / Suggestion

Rather than spending another 25m on a broken model, it would be better to immediately fragment the Agency into  core groups focused on specific and targeted challenges, with each putting forward their own proposals.

It would make more sense if Thom focused on the areas that have been successful and this in turn resulted in a much more focused area where his expertise can be more deeply felt, rather than spreading his talents thinly. 

The first step is a blunt and honest assessment of Edgeware's current status - it's primary issues and areas requiring improvement. We are now in the exciting position of having a wide array of assembled talent and teams who are buillding the network and it's subsidiaries as an emerging hive mind.
